planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Europa is an early-blooming Georg Arends hybrid with soft pink plumes.

directions: Europa is an early-season Georg Arends hybrid astilbe bearing dense, feathery plumes of soft shell-pink flowers held above finely divided, dark green foliage. It blooms ahead of many other Astilbe x arendsii cultivars in late spring to early summer, extending the shade border's bloom season before later selections take over. Give it consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since Astilbe wilts quickly and scorches in dry soil or hot afternoon sun. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous, full plumes.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Diamant (Diamond) is a pure white Georg Arends hybrid blooming in midsummer.

directions: Diamant, meaning diamond, is a pure white-flowered Georg Arends hybrid astilbe, producing dense, upright plumes that glow in a shaded border and pair well with darker-flowered companions. It blooms in midsummer above finely cut, dark green foliage, and the crisp white color holds well without fading or pinking as it ages, unlike some white astilbe selections. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since dry soil quickly causes browning at the plume tips. Divide every three to four years in spring to keep the clump full and floriferous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Etna is a dark red-flowered Georg Arends hybrid with bronze-tinted young foliage.

directions: Etna is a Georg Arends hybrid astilbe named for the volcano, opening dense plumes of deep garnet-red flowers over dark green foliage that emerges with a bronze flush in spring. Its saturated color makes it a strong accent among paler pink and white astilbe cultivars in a mixed shade border, blooming in midsummer. Give it consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since Astilbe declines quickly in dry conditions. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain strong bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Granat (Garnet) is a compact, deep red Georg Arends hybrid.

directions: Granat, German for garnet, is a compact Georg Arends hybrid astilbe bearing tight, deep garnet-red plumes over dark, glossy green foliage, staying lower and more restrained than many arendsii cultivars. Its compact habit suits it to the front of a shaded border or a container planting where taller astilbe would be out of scale. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and mulch to help retain the even moisture this genus requires. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain a dense, floriferous clump.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Spinell (Spinel) is a salmon-pink Georg Arends hybrid named for the gemstone.

directions: Spinell, named for the gemstone, is a Georg Arends hybrid astilbe bearing warm salmon-pink plumes over finely divided dark green foliage, blooming in midsummer. Its warmer pink tone sets it apart from the cooler rose and lilac-pink shades common among arendsii astilbe, making it a useful color-bridging plant in a mixed border. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; dry soil quickly causes the plumes to brown at the tips. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.

common_name: Professor van der Wielen Astilbe (Tall White Thunbergii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; this tall thunbergii selection has gracefully arching flower sprays rather than the stiffly upright plumes typical of arendsii hybrids.

directions: Professor van der Wielen is a tall, old Astilbe thunbergii selection known for airy, gracefully arching sprays of small white flowers held well above the foliage on strong stems, a looser, more informal effect than the dense, upright plumes of arendsii hybrids. Reaching 3 to 4 feet in bloom, it makes a dramatic architectural accent at the back of a shaded border or near water, where its drooping flower sprays can be appreciated from below. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since thunbergii types are if anything less tolerant of dry soil than arendsii hybrids. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: Great Plant Picks (Elisabeth C. Miller Botanical Garden)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Anita Pfeifer is an older Georg Arends hybrid with coral-pink plumes and bronze-tinged foliage.

directions: Anita Pfeifer is an older Georg Arends hybrid astilbe bearing warm coral-pink plumes over dark green foliage tinged bronze when young, blooming in midsummer above the clump. Its distinctive coral tone, warmer than the typical rose-pinks of the arendsii group, gives it a useful place in a shaded border planned around warm color schemes. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and mulch to buffer soil moisture through summer heat. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain strong bloom.
